card.name: Verbs in old historical narrative
card.fires_on: Words in older-style historical prose (wars, legislatures, explorers, quotations), often a past-tense verb or small word right after a subject, such as burnt, passed, voted, made.

modes.label: Past-tense verb after subject
modes.description: A past-tense action verb follows a group or institution in a historical account.
modes.example: In the year 1818, as we have seen stated in other chapters of this work, Congress<< passed>> a joint resolution organizing the Territory of Missouri

modes.label: Opening word of a quotation
modes.description: The first word inside a quote or remark in old writing, such as A or Let.

modes.label: Small word mid-clause
modes.description: A short word like a, the or no inside an archaic-style sentence.
modes.example: As Adam Smith put it, "There is<< a>> lot of ruin in a nation."
